images.title: Two triangles: turned or flipped
images.purpose: Before and after: two copies of a 6 cm, 9 cm, 12 cm triangle joined along the 12 cm side, turned half round to make a parallelogram, or flipped over to make a kite.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two panels side by side with plenty of space between them: on the left the parallelogram, on the right the kite.
images.exact_structure: Both panels use two copies of one triangle with sides 6, 9 and 12 units, one copy lightly filled teal (#0072B2) and the other lightly filled amber (#E69F00), joined along their 12 unit side, which is drawn as a dashed grey (#6B7280) line. Left panel: the amber copy is turned half round, so the outline is a parallelogram with sides 6, 9, 6, 9 going round; label 6 cm on one 6 unit side, 9 cm on one 9 unit side, 12 cm on the dashed join, and the word parallelogram under the panel. Right panel: the amber copy is flipped over the 12 unit side, mirror image of the teal one, so the outline is a kite with sides 6, 6, 9, 9 going round and the two 6 unit sides next to each other; label 6 cm on one 6 unit side, 9 cm on one 9 unit side, and the word kite under the panel. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Turning the second triangle gives a parallelogram; flipping it gives a kite.
images.description: Before and after: two copies of a 6 cm, 9 cm, 12 cm triangle joined along the 12 cm side, turned half round to make a parallelogram, or flipped over to make a kite.
images.context: 6 + 9 > 12, so the triangle exists; the angles at the ends of the 12 cm side are acute, so the kite on that side does not cave in.

image_decisions.why: Comparing turned and flipped on the same side shows where the two families of shapes come from.
